method: Independently construed actual public Old English; no draft key or design private witness consulted. Public example glosses were visible as part of the input and independently checked, not treated as proof.

examples.text: Ðā se fiscere cōm, ðā sæt se sunu on ðǣm hūse.
examples.independent_translation: When the fisherman came, then the son sat in the house.

examples.text: Ðonne se munuc cymð, ðonne sęlð se mann him męte.
examples.independent_translation: Whenever the monk comes, then the man gives him food.

examples.text: Ðā-hwīle-ðe se munuc sang, se sunu dranc wæter.
examples.independent_translation: While the monk sang, the son drank water.

examples.text: Mid-ðȳ se sunu ǣt, se fæder sæt on ðǣm hūse.
examples.independent_translation: While the son ate, the father sat in the house.

examples.text: Ne farað, ǣr se munuc cume.
examples.independent_translation: Do not go (you plural) before the monk comes.
Be (you singular) here until we come.

examples.text: Se mann healp ðǣm cuman, for-ðon-ðe hē wæs untrum.
examples.independent_translation: The man helped the stranger because he was sick. The stipulated he is the stranger; the morphology alone does not identify his antecedent.

examples.text: Ic cume, ðæt ic ðē helpe.
examples.independent_translation: I come so that I may help you (singular).

examples.text: Se fæder cōm, ðæt hē his suna hulpe.
examples.independent_translation: The father came so that he might help his son.

examples.text: Heald ðæt dēor, ðȳ-lǣs-ðe hit ðone męte nime.
examples.independent_translation: Hold the animal, lest it take the food.

examples.text: Se sunu wæs swā glæd, ðæt hē sang.
examples.independent_translation: The son was so glad that he sang.

examples.text: Ðēah se fiscere sīe eald, hē hilpð his suna.
examples.independent_translation: Although the fisherman is old, he helps his son.

examples.text: Gif se munuc is hēr, hē hilpð ðǣm męnn.
examples.independent_translation: If the monk is here, he helps the man.

examples.text: Gif se munuc wǣre hēr, hē hulpe ðǣm męnn.
examples.independent_translation: If the monk were here (he is absent now), he would help the man.

compositions.text: Se ealda fiscere cōm tō ðǣm hūse, ðæt hē his suna hulpe. Ðā hē cōm, ðā wæs se sunu hungrig. Se fiscere sealde him męte. Mid-ðȳ se sunu ǣt, se fiscere bær wæter. Ðēah se fiscere wǣre eald, hē healp his suna. Se sunu cwæð: “Wes hēr, oð-ðæt ic cume.” Hē gewāt and cōm and sealde his fæder wæter.
compositions.independent_translation: The old fisherman came to the house so that he might help his son. When he came, the son was hungry. The fisherman gave him food. While the son ate, the fisherman carried water. Although the fisherman was old, he helped his son. The son said, “Be here until I come.” He went away and came back and gave his father water.
compositions.reference_note: First hē refers contextually to the fisherman; first him is the son. Last Hē is naturally the son, continuing his stated coming; his fæder is the fisherman. The pronoun morphology permits more than one masculine antecedent, so the key must distinguish contextual coherence from uniquely determined inflection. Back in came back expresses the context, not a separate lexical return prefix.
